text.p: These are the leading stories in Zimbabwe's state-owned Herald newspaper on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Legislators from Zimbabwe's ruling ZANU-PF party stayed away from a crucial meeting earlier this week which had been intended to push them into approving loans to fund Harare's new international airport terminal set to cost Z$1.2 billion.

- South African foreign minister Alfred Nzo said in Harare on Wednesday his country had granted citizenship to five spies jailed for life in Zimbabwe for acts of sabotage during the era of apartheid. He said President Nelson Mandela had asked for the men's release during talks with his Zimbabwean counterpart Robert Mugabe.

- Top government and ZANU-PF officials have abandoned plans to launch a judicial commission to investigate widespread looting of the country's War Victims Compensation Fund, worried that such a probe could inflict irreparable damage on the party's image and that of the government.

- The head of Zimbabwe's government tender board Stanley Mahlahla disclosed this week that cabinet secretary Charles Utete had ordered him to reverse an original decision by the board to jointly award the country's second cellular phone licence to telecommunications companies Econet and Telecel, instead solely awarding it to the latter.

- The privatisation of government-owned dairy company, Dairibord Zimbabwe Limited, starts next month and several categories of shareholders have been lined up to stake a claim in a total of 252.5 million shares which will be offered through a private placing.

- Hundreds of labour disputes remain unresolved in Zimbabwe owing to bureaucracy at the Labour Relations Tribunal and there are now fears that this could worsen working relations between employees and employers.

- Integration of world economies through trade and financial flows has posed a challenge for Southern African economies to formulate economic policies that will make the region a more attractive target for foreign investors.

- Zimbabwe's electric power utility, ZESA and British-based company National Power International have signed a letter of intent to develop Sengwa Power Station in central Zimbabwe, a move geared to bolster Zimbabwe's power supply.
